name: Sicilian Najdorf — White Tactics
description: 4 strategic challenges for White in the Najdorf 6.Bg5 line. Find the right plan after 8...Qc7!

drills.name: Castle and Develop
drills.description: White gets the king to safety with O-O, then develops the critical c1 bishop to e3.
drills.briefExplanation: White castles kingside for safety, then brings Bc1 to the critical e3 square.
drills.explanation: O-O is the natural first step — the king belongs behind the pawn shelter on g1. After Black mirrors with O-O, White plays Be3, finally developing the c1 bishop to its ideal square. From e3, the bishop supports the Nd4, controls the d4-h7 diagonal, and clears the way for eventual O-O-O in future positions. In the Najdorf 6.Bg5 structure, Be3 is the cornerstone of the 'English Attack' setup — it activates the passive Bc1 and connects the rooks.

drills.name: The f5 Pawn Break
drills.description: White launches the critical f4-f5 advance to rip open the kingside, then removes Black's key defender.
drills.briefExplanation: White smashes open the kingside with f5. After exf5, Bxf6 eliminates Black's key defender.
drills.explanation: f5 is the signature Najdorf attacking break. The pawn on f5 jabs into Black's pawn chain, forcing exf5 (otherwise White plays fxe6 with a dangerous passed pawn). After exf5, White plays Bxf6 — trading the Bg5 for the Nf6. This removes Black's most active defensive piece, doubles or weakens the kingside pawns, and leaves Black's king exposed after ...gxf6 or ...Bxf6. The f-file can be opened later with fxe5 or e5 breaks. This is the most direct attacking approach — White commits to a full-scale kingside storm.

drills.name: Central Pawn Advance
drills.description: White strikes in the center with e5, and after the recapture reclaims with fxe5 — a powerful pawn wedge.
drills.briefExplanation: White plays e5 to challenge the center. After dxe5, White recaptures with fxe5 — creating a powerful advanced pawn.
drills.explanation: e5 immediately challenges Black's d6 pawn — the anchor of the Najdorf structure. After dxe5 (forced, or the d6 pawn hangs), White plays fxe5, establishing a dominant e5-pawn that attacks the Nf6 directly. The Nf6 is now under threat — it must retreat or be lost. The open f-file becomes a rook highway for White's kingside attack. With the e5-pawn cramps Black's entire position, restricting the Ne7 and Be7. This is White's most space-grabbing approach.

drills.name: The English Attack Setup
drills.description: White plays Be3 to activate the bishop, then castles queenside to launch a full-board assault.
drills.briefExplanation: Be3 develops the bishop and clears the queenside. After Black castles, White castles queenside — the classic opposite-sides-castling Najdorf war.
drills.explanation: Be3 is the key preparatory move. It develops the passive Bc1 to an active square, controls the a7-g1 diagonal, and — critically — clears the c1 square so White can castle queenside. After Black plays O-O (castling into safety), White plays O-O-O, the defining move of the English Attack (Be3 + f3 + g4-g5 system). Now both kings are on opposite wings, and the race begins: White storms the kingside, Black attacks the queenside. This opposite-castling structure is the heart of Najdorf complexity — whoever attacks faster wins.
